thread:
Maya: Heads-up — staging-rt saw steady memory increase during a long streaming tool loop run. ~180MB/hr for ~6hrs before OOM on one job. Not typical short-run leak patterns. :thinking_face:
Alex: Interesting — did this start after the recent kernel selection change? we switched to the fused-token kernels for <32 seq lengths last week.
Sam: I reproduced locally with the `long_stream_repro.py` script. runs: `./scripts/long_stream_repro.py --workers 4 --iters 20000 --profile` on commit `b7f2a1`. Heap growth matches staging.
Katie: quick jemalloc snapshot from Sam's run: 
```
jemalloc stats: active: 2.6G -> 3.4G over 6h
slab: kv_pages: +4200 slots
small: stable
```
Looks like a KV page residency growth, not general allocator churn.
Alex: pprof of runtime heap shows most retained objects are `KVPage` + `PinnedSpan` pairs. The refcounts on those pages never drop to zero. Suspect eviction path not triggered for pages reused by streaming toolloops.
Maya: I captured a short trace with `runtime/traces` and grep'd for `evict` calls — eviction attempted but skipped because `last_access_tick` < eviction_threshold due to tick scaling with batches. In other words, bigger batch agg => tick jumps, windows don't align.
dev-bot: uploaded flamegraph: https://artifacts/redwood/fg/4979990000-kv-erosion.svg :eyes:
Alex: that explains kernel selection angle: fused kernels increase per-batch token density, so KV pages get referenced more frequently in a time window and never fall into the eviction window. Eviction policy assumed roughly uniform token arrival; streaming toolloops break that assumption.
Sam: I instrumented and added a `pinned_by_stream` bool to debug — pages used by active long-session streams keep a different refcount that the general eviction path ignores. Quick hack lowering `evict_window_ticks` from 3000 -> 800 reduced residency in my run by ~65%.
Katie: lowering window helps but feels brittle. Could we instead track per-stream LRU timestamp and prefer evicting pages not touched by any active long session?
Jia: I can run a 48h soak on dedicated-2 with the window tweak and the new per-stream metric `kv.pages.active_streams`. If pass, propose a canary behind `feature.kv_adaptive_eviction`.
Alex: Also worth checking that batching heuristic isn't pinning pages because we coalesce requests aggressively. Proposal: add a max-pin-duration that scales with sequence-length histogram, and expose metric `kv.page.pin_duration_p99`.
Maya: Agreed. Next steps: Sam to open a minimal PR with the `evict_window` flag + metrics. Alex to prototype adaptive eviction heuristic. Jia to run soak with flag on dedicated. Katie to add an alert `kv.page_residency_growth>200MB/hr for 2h`.
Sam: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/1234 — contains repro script, debug counters, and `--evict-window` runtime flag.
Maya: Perfect. Putting this on triage board. If canary looks good, we should roll to staging for 24h and then to prod canary 5% traffic. :thumbsup:
Alex: one more note — check kernel-selection telemetry (we added `kernel.selection` tag) to correlate pinned runs with `fused_small_seq` entries. If correlation strong, we may add a kernel-aware eviction override.
Jia: starting soak now. I’ll post results in this thread. :memo:
